title: Things to Do in Bukit Bintang from Lalaport BBCC
metaDescription: Things to do in Bukit Bintang when you arrive at Lalaport: the malls, Jalan Alor, Changkat and KLCC, and the Monorail, MRT, van or Grab to each.

contentBlocks.content: Things to do in Bukit Bintang start the moment you leave Lalaport. The district is KL's shopping and nightlife centre: Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, Lot 10, Sungei Wang, Berjaya Times Square, the food stalls of Jalan Alor and the bars of Changkat Bukit Bintang (Tourism Malaysia). If you arrived by coach at the Lalaport Transportation Hub, you are one train ride away. The Monorail from Hang Tuah station reaches Bukit Bintang station in two stops.
This guide lists what to see and do, and how to get to each place from Lalaport by Monorail, MRT, van or Grab.
Key Takeaways
How do I get from Lalaport to Bukit Bintang? Take the Monorail from Hang Tuah station two stops, through Imbi, to Bukit Bintang station.
What should I do first? Walk the malls by day, then eat on Jalan Alor or drink on Changkat Bukit Bintang at night.
Can I walk to KLCC? Yes. From Pavilion, an air conditioned walkway runs about 1 km to the Petronas Twin Towers.
What do I do with my luggage? Leave it in a locker at the Lalaport hub. There are 36, from RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours.
Getting around from Lalaport

Sources: Hang Tuah walk and BOLEH BOLEH Ride fares from LaLaport BBCC; Merdeka exit from BusOnlineTicket. Buy train tokens at the station machines by card or cash. Tourism Malaysia notes that international visitors can buy a KL Travel Pass for unlimited rides on the Monorail, LRT and MRT.
Got bags? Lock them up at the hub first. Our Lalaport Transportation Hub guide covers the lockers and the way to the train.
Shop the Bukit Bintang malls
Pavilion Kuala Lumpur

Pavilion has more than 700 shops, from international labels to local brands (Tourism Malaysia). The Food Republic food court is on Level 1, and DADI Cinema is inside. From Pavilion you can walk about 1 km to KLCC and the Petronas Twin Towers along an air conditioned route (The Straits Times). Take the MRT to Pavilion Kuala Lumpur Bukit Bintang MRT, or the Monorail to Bukit Bintang.
Lot 10

Lot 10 has stood at the main Bukit Bintang junction since 1990, with its green facade, an H&M flagship and Isetan The Japan Store (Tourism Malaysia). Go down to Lot 10 Hutong in the basement for more than 30 hawker stalls; it is non-halal. Go up to J's Gate Dining on the top floor for 17 Japanese restaurants. Get off the Monorail at Bukit Bintang station.
Sungei Wang Plaza and Low Yat

Sungei Wang opened in 1977 and has more than 600 tenants selling fashion, electronics, beauty products and souvenirs. Low Yat is the gadget mall, with phone and computer shops on every floor (Tourism Malaysia). Get off at Bukit Bintang station and follow the mall signs.
Berjaya Times Square

Berjaya Times Square has more than 1,000 shops across a 48 storey building, plus a hotel and an indoor amusement park (Tourism Malaysia). Set it as your Grab destination, or check the station signs on the Monorail.
LaLaport BBCC

Do not skip the mall you arrived in. LaLaport BBCC has around 300 shops, restaurants and entertainment outlets (LaLaport BBCC), a floor for anime, comics and games, and a cinema (The Straits Times). It is the easy choice for a rainy afternoon or a long wait for your coach.
Eat in Bukit Bintang

Jalan Alor is the famous one: seafood restaurants, hawker stalls and coffee shops that light up at night. Our supper guide covers Jalan Alor late at night, and the Bukit Bintang food guide goes street by street. Here are four places in our directory within the district.
Kuro Ramen, on the 4th floor of Lot 10, serves tonkotsu ramen in a pork broth developed by its Japanese owner, Akira Nagata.
TORIGEN Chicken Ramen, also on the 4th floor of Lot 10 in J's Gate Dining, makes its ramen with a rich chicken broth. It is pork-free, with no lard and no alcohol.

Kampachi Pavilion, on Level 6 of Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, was the first Kampachi outside the Equatorial Hotel. It serves Japanese food with ingredients from Japan, including seafood from Toyosu Market in Tokyo.
Kusa Japanese Vegan Restaurant is on Lorong Ceylon, a walk from Bukit Bintang Monorail station, and serves Japanese vegan food.
Want more? Browse the restaurant directory and filter by area.
Go out on Changkat Bukit Bintang

Changkat Bukit Bintang is the bar street, a short walk from Jalan Alor. Expect lounges, bars, live bands and DJs, and outdoor tables (Tourism Malaysia). Take the Monorail to Bukit Bintang and walk, and book a Grab back to your hotel when you are done.
Further afield by train from Hang Tuah

• Petaling Street and Chinatown. One stop on the LRT to Plaza Rakyat. Try fried Hokkien mee, beef noodle soup or halal hand pulled mee tarik (The Straits Times).
  • Sultan Abdul Samad Building and Merdeka Square. Two stops on the LRT to Masjid Jamek.
  • KLCC and the Petronas Twin Towers. Monorail or MRT to Bukit Bintang, then the walkway from Pavilion.
Planning a day out of the city? Our Genting Highlands day trip guide covers going by private driver.
Leaving Bukit Bintang

When it is time to go, you leave from where you arrived. The Lalaport hub has airport buses and coaches back to Singapore. See our guides to Bukit Bintang to KLIA2 and the KL to Singapore bus, or go straight to the Lalaport to Bugis coach.

contentBlocks.content: Frequently Asked Questions
How do I get from Lalaport to Bukit Bintang?
To get from Lalaport to Bukit Bintang, take the KL Monorail from Hang Tuah station two stops, through Imbi, to Bukit Bintang station. You can also take the BOLEH BOLEH Ride van for RM4 or a Grab.
What is there to do in Bukit Bintang at night?
At night in Bukit Bintang, eat at the stalls and restaurants on Jalan Alor, then walk to the bars of Changkat Bukit Bintang. The big malls keep normal mall hours.
Can I walk from Bukit Bintang to KLCC?
Yes. You can walk from Bukit Bintang to KLCC along an air conditioned walkway from Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, about 1 km, to the Petronas Twin Towers.
Where can I leave my luggage in Bukit Bintang?
You can leave luggage at the Lalaport Transportation Hub, which has 36 lockers from RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours. You can open yours as often as you need within that time.
Conclusion

The things to do in Bukit Bintang are two Monorail stops from Lalaport: the malls by day, Jalan Alor and Changkat by night, and KLCC on foot from Pavilion. Leave your bags at the hub, buy a token at Hang Tuah, and go. When your trip ends, book your bus from Lalaport to KLIA2 on ttklia.com.
